title: Oct 10 Results + Oct 11 Preview: Perfect Start to the Postseason
summary: Nailed the Guardians pick at 53%. Tomorrow: Brewers host Dodgers in a pitcher's duel.

content.value:
## A Clean Sweep to Start October

You know, I've been doing this long enough to appreciate a perfect day when it comes. October 10th gave us just that—a clean 1-0 record with the Guardians coming through at Progressive Field. Nothing flashy, just solid baseball and a model that caught the right side of a close one.

## The Guardians Did What They Do

The Sox-Guardians matchup wasn't a coin flip, but it was close—53% confidence on Cleveland. I've seen enough October baseball to know that home field in a tight series can be the difference, and the Guardians have been playing fundamental baseball all season. They didn't need to blow anyone away; they just needed to execute, and they did.

That's postseason baseball in a nutshell. The margins are razor-thin, and the team that makes fewer mistakes usually punches their ticket to the next round.

## Tomorrow's Spotlight: Dodgers at Brewers

Now we turn our attention to October 11, and this one's got some juice. The Dodgers head to Milwaukee, and our model is leaning Brewers at 61% confidence. What makes this interesting is the pitching matchup we're looking at.

## The Pitching Matchup That Has My Attention

Tarik Skubal on the mound for Los Angeles is no joke—the guy's been one of the best arms in baseball. But here's the thing: Jacob Misiorowski at home in Milwaukee is a different animal. I've seen enough of these playoff series to know that young arms with something to prove in front of their home crowd can rise to the occasion.

The Brewers have been excellent at American Family Field this year, and that 61% confidence from the model reflects not just Misiorowski's ability, but the entire ecosystem around him—the defense, the bullpen depth, and that crowd energy that can rattle even the most experienced visitors.

Skubal's got the pedigree, sure. But October has a way of leveling the playing field. The Brewers aren't going to be intimidated by a big name, and that home cooking could be the edge they need.

## What I'm Watching

Here's what'll determine this one: early run support and pitch efficiency. If Misiorowski can work efficiently through five or six innings and hand it to Milwaukee's bullpen with a lead, the Brewers are in excellent shape. On the flip side, if Skubal finds his groove early and the Dodgers can manufacture runs the way they're capable of, that 61% can flip in a hurry.

I've seen this script before—powerful visiting team, confident home underdog, October atmosphere. It usually comes down to who executes in the middle innings. That's where games are won and lost this time of year.

Stay sharp, and let's see if we can keep this momentum rolling into Saturday.

author: Max
